capabilities.types_formats: CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL/NDJSON, Vortex, Parquet, Arrow IPC/Feather, Avro and ORC
capabilities.artifact_requirement: Published CLI or Python wheel; source builds need the matching format features
capabilities.restriction: Local paths only. Reader options and representable types depend on the format; remote catalogs and transactions are separate work.

capabilities.types_formats: Iceberg v1/v2, supported Delta profiles and Hudi Copy-on-Write v8/v9
capabilities.artifact_requirement: 1.1.0 CLI or Python wheel with local table readers
capabilities.restriction: Select the table format and a supported snapshot of local Parquet data. The reader applies table-specific visibility and schema rules before execution.

capabilities.operation: Filter, project, aggregate, join, compute windows and order
capabilities.types_formats: Admitted typed scalar and static nested inputs
capabilities.restriction: SQL and DataFrame operations compose within the supported type and operator contracts. Named SQL parameters bind scalar values. Query-local relations bind DataFrames.
Small computed-result collection is limited to 65,536 rows and 8 MiB. Use batches or a writer for larger admitted results. Python object conversion allocates separately.

capabilities.types_formats: Admitted finite results and explicitly typed finite producers
capabilities.artifact_requirement: Linux or macOS Python wheel; native columnar ownership requires a native wheel
capabilities.restriction: Full drain and final success establish completion. Process batch pipes require POSIX; Windows users should use collection or a writer. Process frames contain at most 2,048 rows and 8 MiB. A yielded batch does not certify later input.

capabilities.types_formats: Vortex, CSV, JSON, JSONL, Parquet, Arrow IPC, Avro and ORC
capabilities.artifact_requirement: Published CLI or Python wheel with the matching writer
capabilities.restriction: Use a new destination. CSV writes nested values as JSON text. ORC supports admitted decimal, list, struct, date and timestamp values. Each destination has its own commit and readback.

capabilities.operation: Reuse a native result as input
capabilities.types_formats: Admitted ShardLoom-owned arrays and exact schemas
capabilities.artifact_requirement: Linux or macOS native Python wheel; transport=native
capabilities.restriction: Use ctx.from_result(result) for native owned data without an Arrow export. Completed results remain usable after context close. Cross-owner admission may copy under the receiving grant; process results use a bounded typed payload.

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
import shardloom as sl

workspace = TemporaryDirectory(prefix="shardloom-orders-")
orders = Path(workspace.name) / "orders.csv"
orders.write_text("order_id,status\n1,paid\n2,pending\n3,paid\n", encoding="utf-8")

# Illustrative caller choices: 256 MiB and two execution lanes.
ctx = sl.context(transport="native", memory_bytes=256 << 20, max_parallelism=2)

).collect(check=True)

examples.pythonExample:
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
import shardloom as sl

workspace = TemporaryDirectory(prefix="shardloom-orders-")
orders = Path(workspace.name) / "orders.csv"
orders.write_text("order_id,status\n1,paid\n2,pending\n3,paid\n", encoding="utf-8")

# Illustrative caller choices: 256 MiB and two execution lanes.
ctx = sl.context(transport="native", memory_bytes=256 << 20, max_parallelism=2)

paid = ctx.read_csv(orders).filter(sl.col("status") == "paid").sort("order_id")
result = paid.collect(check=True)
print(result.to_rows())

ctx.close()
workspace.cleanup()

examples.cliExample:
workspace="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$workspace"' EXIT
printf '%s' 'order_id,status
1,paid
2,pending
3,paid
' > "$workspace/orders.csv"
shardloom run sql --input "$workspace/orders.csv" \
  --sql "SELECT order_id, status FROM '$workspace/orders.csv' WHERE status = 'paid' ORDER BY order_id" \
  --request collect --bounded true --memory-bytes 268435456 --max-parallelism 2 --format json
